title: 188. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Solving Two-by-Two Linear Systems by Substitution
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Solving a two-by-two linear system by substitution
questions.learningObjective: Solve a two-variable linear system by substituting one equation into the other.
questions.question: Solve the system \(x+y=7,\quad y=x-1\) by substitution.
questions.hint: Replace \(y\) in the first equation with the expression \(x-1\), then solve for \(x\).

questions.concept: Substitution with one variable already isolated
questions.learningObjective: Use an isolated variable to solve a linear system by substitution.
questions.question: Solve the system \(y=2x+1,\quad 3x+y=11\) by substitution.
questions.hint: Use the first equation to replace \(y\) in the second equation.

questions.concept: Substitution when one variable is expressed in terms of the other
questions.learningObjective: Substitute an expression for \(x\) into a second linear equation and determine the solution.
questions.question: Solve the system \(x=3y-4,\quad 2x-y=7\) by substitution.
questions.hint: Replace \(x\) in the second equation with \(3y-4\), then solve for \(y\).

questions.concept: Substitution with a simple linear expression
questions.learningObjective: Solve a two-by-two linear system by substituting \(y=x-3\).
questions.question: Solve the system \(3x+y=13,\quad y=x-3\) by substitution.
questions.hint: Replace \(y\) in the first equation with \(x-3\).

questions.concept: Evaluating an expression after solving by substitution
questions.learningObjective: Solve a linear system by substitution and compute a related expression.
questions.question: For the system \(2x+3y=12,\quad x=y+1\), what is the value of \(x+y\)?
questions.hint: First solve the system for \(x\) and \(y\), then compute \(x+y\).

questions.learningObjective: Solve a linear system by substituting \(y=4-x\) into the other equation.
questions.question: Solve the system \(y=4-x,\quad 3x-2y=7\) by substitution.
questions.hint: Replace \(y\) in the second equation with \(4-x\), then solve for \(x\).

questions.concept: Determining a parameter in a linear system using a given solution
questions.learningObjective: Use substitution of a given ordered pair to find an unknown coefficient.
questions.question: The ordered pair \((2,1)\) is a solution of the system \(kx+y=7,\quad x+y=3\). What is \(k\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute \(x=2\) and \(y=1\) into \(kx+y=7\): \(k(2)+1=7\), so \(2k=6\), \(k=3\). The second equation is also satisfied: \(2+1=3\). Therefore \(k=3\).
questions.hint: Substitute the given \(x\)- and \(y\)-values into the first equation and solve for \(k\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the number of solutions of a linear system by substitution.
questions.question: Solve the system \(y=2x+3,\quad 4x-2y=-6\) by substitution. How many solutions does the system have?
questions.explanation: Substitute \(y=2x+3\) into \(4x-2y=-6\): \(4x-2(2x+3)=-6\), so \(4x-4x-6=-6\), which simplifies to \(-6=-6\). This is always true, so the two equations represent the same line. The system has infinitely many solutions.
questions.hint: After substitution, simplify both sides. If the variable disappears, decide whether the remaining numerical statement is true or false.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a linear system involving a fraction by substitution.
questions.question: Solve the system \(\frac{x}{2}+y=5,\quad x-y=1\) by substitution.
questions.hint: First express \(x\) in terms of \(y\) from the second equation, then substitute into the first.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a linear system by substitution and evaluate a linear expression of the solution.
questions.question: Solve the system \(x+2y=8,\quad 3x-y=3\) by substitution. What is the value of \(2x+y\)?
questions.hint: Solve for one variable first using substitution, then evaluate \(2x+y\) with the ordered pair.
